You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

<sentences>
S1: Bruce Ward is a pleasant 60-year-old male who presents to the clinic today following a positive result in a hepatitis C antibody test.
S2: The patient will follow up with me in 3 weeks to review his results and discuss further treatment.
S3: Bowel sounds are present.
S4: He notes he used to smoke more and is having difficulty with complete cessation.
S5: He was sent to obtain the hepatitis C antibody test as part of a routine physical.
S6: I have also recommended that we obtain an ultrasound elastography to evaluate for fibrosis of the liver.
S7: CONSTITUTIONAL: In no apparent distress.
S8: The patient reports smoking 1 to 2 cigarettes per day.
S9: The patient is married with children and is concerned about their hepatitis C status.
S10: His initial labs were consistent with a hepatitis C diagnosis.
S11: RESPIRATORY: Lungs are clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
S12: The HCV antibody test was reviewed today and is positive.
S13: I advised the patient that his family should be screened and we will assist him with setting appointments with their primary care physician.
S14: I have recommended that we confirm the diagnosis with additional blood work including checking his hepatitis C RNA and HCV genotype.
S15: Patient denies taking any current medications.
S16: Liver panel revealed an elevated AST at 39 U/L.
S17: The patient is married with children.
S18: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur is appreciated.
S19: The patient denies any significant past medical history.
S20: The patient admits to intravenous drug use in the past; however, he notes it has been longer than 15 years since his last usage.
S21: He reports history of IV drug use 15 years ago.
S22: He states he is anxious with the results and denies he has ever been diagnosed with hepatitis C.
S23: After reviewing the patient's laboratory findings today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him in regard to his current symptoms.
S24: He currently drinks beer occasionally.
S25: He continues to drink a beer on occasion.
S26: He reports a family history of high blood pressure, diabetes, and depression.
S27: He also reports a history of heavy alcohol use.
S28: The patient currently smokes 1 to 2 cigarettes per day.
S29: CV: Regular rate and rhythm.
S30: GI/GU: Abdomen is soft with no hepatosplenomegaly.
S31: The ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin were all within normal limits.
</sentences>
